about: One table, run twice: by tests/agent-state.test.js and tests/turn-events.test.js, and by aify-comms service/tests/test_the_ported_turn_law_agrees.py through the Python they port. Times are seconds before a fixed now (null = no timestamp); event times are microseconds. 'owner' is a lifetime here and a registered machine id in aify-comms. In hookOrder, 'accept' is today's Python answer and 'aifyEnv' is aify-env's (admission, then ordering within one lifetime); a row where they differ names why in 'divergence'.

turnLaw.name: a re-stamping poster cannot postpone an unverified turn
verified, renews against the last renewal
a future start does not hold
verified, a future touch falls back to a recent start
verified, a future touch falls back to an old start
verified, a touch older than the start is ignored
unverified, a row from before the start anchor uses its touch

hookOrder.name: no time: outside the ordering
hookOrder.divergence: every 0.9 sender stamps firedAtUs; an end that cannot be ordered could close a newer turn

hookOrder.name: earlier, same owner: a slow start after its own end
a tie goes to the end
the first event of a new owner, whatever its clock
a delayed event from a previous owner
an event naming no owner is not refused by the owner check
hookOrder.divergence: C4 adopts a resident only from its lifetime record, so an event naming none has no turn here (review of 591d172f, R1)

hookOrder.name: no owner registered yet
hookOrder.divergence: C4: no verified lifetime, no turn

hookOrder.name: an unbound end earlier than the bound turn's last event (R1)
hookOrder.divergence: today's owner-change branch takes it as the first event of a new owner and closes the bound turn
